title: Shakshuka
subtitle: Eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce
excerpt: Eggs poached directly in a spiced, garlicky tomato and pepper sauce. A dish eaten across North Africa and the Levant for breakfast, brunch, or a quick supper.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shakshuka is widespread across North Africa and the Levant, with the name itself of Arabic or Berber origin. Tunisia, Israel, Libya, Egypt, and Yemen all claim versions of the dish, with variations in spicing and ingredients.

recipeTools.notes: A deep frying pan or wide shallow casserole with a lid.

content.text: Shakshuka is eggs poached in a thick, spiced tomato and pepper sauce in a single pan. The whites set in the sauce while the yolks stay runny, and the whole thing is scooped up with bread. It takes about 30 minutes and feeds two from one pan.

Heat the oil in a large, deep frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and pepper. Cook for 8 minutes until very soft. Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and chilli flakes. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and tomato puree. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened and is no longer watery.

Make four wells in the sauce using the back of a spoon. Crack an egg into each well. Cover the pan and cook over a low to medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Scatter over the parsley and feta if using. Serve straight from the pan with flatbreads or crusty bread.
